newsitem.title: USA: Texaco gathers team to investigate plant fire.
newsitem.headline: Texaco gathers team to investigate plant fire.

text.p: Texaco Inc said on Tuesday it assembled a team to begin investigating the cause of Monday's large fire at its Wilmington, California refinery in the Los Angeles area.
"They're having their first meetings this morning," a Texaco spokeswoman said.

She said the team includes an outside consultant, plant employees, other company experts and representatives from the Oil, Chemical, and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW), the union which represents plant workers.

Monday's fire began in the plant's Number 4 hydrotreater, a device which removes sulfur compounds and upgrades crude oil in the refining process. News helicopters transmitted images of blackened, twisted metal wreckage in the stricken section.
The damaged hydrotreater handles about 33,000 barrels-per-day of oil, the spokeswoman said.
The plant, with an overall capacity 96,000 bpd, will continue making gasoline and other refined products, the spokeswoman said.
"There's a lot of flexibility with our refinery," she said, adding the plant has three other hydrotreaters.
Wholesale Los Angeles gasoline prices rose up to $0.02/gallon as refiners tried locking up supply after the fire. was reported.
